import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reconstruction conjecture

The *deck* of a finite graph $G$ is the multiset of isomorphism classes of the vertex-deleted
subgraphs $G - v$, one for each vertex $v$ of $G$. The reconstruction conjecture of Kelly and
Ulam says that a graph on at least three vertices is determined, up to isomorphism, by its deck.

The analogous statement for digraphs is false (Stockmeyer). The new digraph reconstruction
conjecture of Ramachandran instead attaches to each card $D - v$ the degree pair
$(\deg^{+}(v), \deg^{-}(v))$ of the deleted vertex, and says that every finite digraph is
determined, up to isomorphism, by this degree-associated deck.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *New digraph reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_digraph_reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- P. J. Kelly, *A congruence theorem for trees*, Pacific J. Math. 7 (1957), 961–968.
- S. Ramachandran, *On a new digraph reconstruction conjecture*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B
  31 (1981), 143–149.
- B. D. McKay, *Reconstruction of small graphs and digraphs*, Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022),
  [arXiv:2102.01942](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01942).
-/

namespace ReconstructionConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/- ## Graphs

A *card* of a graph `G` is a vertex-deleted subgraph `G.induce {v}ᶜ`. Two finite graphs have the
same deck (the same multiset of isomorphism classes of cards) exactly when there is a bijection
`σ` between their vertex sets with `G - v ≅ H - σ v` for every vertex `v`. This is the classical
definition of hypomorphic graphs, and we take it as the definition. -/

/--
Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if there is a bijection `σ` between their
vertex sets such that the vertex-deleted subgraphs `G - v` and `H - σ v` are isomorphic for
every vertex `v` of `G`. For finite graphs this says exactly that `G` and `H` have the same deck,
i.e. the same multiset of isomorphism classes of vertex-deleted subgraphs.
-/
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ)

/-- Isomorphic graphs are hypomorphic. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.of_iso {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} (φ : G ≃g H) :
    Hypomorphic G H :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_adj_iff⟩⟩⟩

/-- Hypomorphic graphs have the same number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.card_eq [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    (h : Hypomorphic G H) : Fintype.card V = Fintype.card W :=
  let ⟨σ, _⟩ := h
  Fintype.card_congr σ

/--
The two graphs on two vertices (the empty graph and the single edge) are hypomorphic, although
they are not isomorphic. This is why the reconstruction conjecture assumes at least three
vertices.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hypomorphic_bot_top_fin_two :
    Hypomorphic (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  ⟨Equiv.refl _, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.refl _, fun {a b} => by
    obtain rfl : a = b := by
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := a
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := b
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ha hb
      revert v a b
      decide
    simp⟩⟩⟩

/--
**The reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly–Ulam):
any two hypomorphic finite simple graphs on at least three vertices are isomorphic.

That is, a finite simple graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its
deck, the multiset of isomorphism classes of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The hypothesis of at
least three vertices is needed because the two graphs on two vertices have the same deck.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) (hV : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hGH : Hypomorphic G H) : Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

/- ## Digraphs

We use Mathlib's `Digraph`, whose adjacency relation is an arbitrary relation `Adj`. In the
digraph reconstruction problem, digraphs are loopless and have at most one arc for each ordered
pair of vertices (so arcs in both directions between two vertices are allowed); we impose
looplessness as a hypothesis. The vertex-deleted subdigraph `D - v` is the restriction
`Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v)` of `Adj` to the vertices other than `v`, and a digraph isomorphism is a
relation isomorphism `≃r` between adjacency relations. -/

/-- The out-degree of the vertex `v` in the digraph `D`: the number of arcs leaving `v`. -/
noncomputable def outDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard

/-- The in-degree of the vertex `v` in the digraph `D`: the number of arcs entering `v`. -/
noncomputable def inDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj w v}.ncard

/-- In the complete digraph every vertex has out-degree equal to the number of vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_top [Fintype V] (v : V) : outDegree (⊤ : Digraph V) v = Fintype.card V := by
  simp [outDegree, Set.ncard_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]

/-- In the complete digraph every vertex has in-degree equal to the number of vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem inDegree_top [Fintype V] (v : V) : inDegree (⊤ : Digraph V) v = Fintype.card V := by
  simp [inDegree, Set.ncard_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]

/-- Digraph isomorphisms preserve out-degrees. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) (v : V) :
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (φ v) := by
  unfold outDegree
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ φ.injective]
  congr 1
  ext w
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := φ.surjective w
  simp [φ.map_rel_iff]

/-- Digraph isomorphisms preserve in-degrees. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem inDegree_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) (v : V) :
    inDegree D v = inDegree E (φ v) := by
  unfold inDegree
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ φ.injective]
  congr 1
  ext w
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := φ.surjective w
  simp [φ.map_rel_iff]

/--
Two digraphs `D` and `E` have the same **degree-associated deck** if there is a bijection `σ`
between their vertex sets such that, for every vertex `v` of `D`, the vertex-deleted subdigraphs
`D - v` and `E - σ v` are isomorphic and `v` and `σ v` have the same out-degree and the same
in-degree. For finite digraphs this says exactly that the multisets of degree-associated cards
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))`, with `D - v` taken up to isomorphism, coincide.
-/
def DegreeHypomorphic (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v,
    Nonempty (Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) ≃r Subrel E.Adj (· ≠ σ v)) ∧
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (σ v) ∧ inDegree D v = inDegree E (σ v)

/-- Isomorphic digraphs have the same degree-associated deck. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem DegreeHypomorphic.of_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) :
    DegreeHypomorphic D E :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_rel_iff⟩⟩,
    outDegree_relIso φ v, inDegree_relIso φ v⟩⟩

/-- Digraphs with the same degree-associated deck have the same number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem DegreeHypomorphic.card_eq [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W}
    (h : DegreeHypomorphic D E) : Fintype.card V = Fintype.card W :=
  let ⟨σ, _⟩ := h
  Fintype.card_congr σ

/--
**The new digraph reconstruction conjecture** (Ramachandran, 1981):
any two finite loopless digraphs with the same degree-associated deck are isomorphic.

That is, a finite digraph (no loops, at most one arc for each ordered pair of vertices) is
determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of pairs `(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))` over its
vertices `v`, where the card `D - v` is taken up to isomorphism. No lower bound on the number of
vertices is needed. The plain digraph analogue of the reconstruction conjecture, without the
degree pairs, is false (Stockmeyer).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.ii [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) (hD : ∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) (hE : ∀ w, ¬ E.Adj w w)
    (hDE : DegreeHypomorphic D E) : Nonempty (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) := by
  sorry

end ReconstructionConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table correctly identifies the two named conjectures, the multiset (not set) deck for slot i with the ≥3-vertex hypothesis, and the degree-associated deck (not the plain deck) for slot ii. The Wikipedia entry's phrase 'whether a graph is uniquely determined by its vertex-deleted subgraphs' is a question in form but names conjectures with positive assertions, so both slots are stated as plain propositions rather than with answer(sorry), following the repository's convention for conjectures.
modeling_decisions: Deck equality is formalized via the classical hypomorphism bijection (∃ σ : V ≃ W with G − v ≅ H − σ v for all v) rather than by literally building a Multiset of isomorphism classes. For finite graphs this is equivalent to equality of the multisets of isomorphism classes of cards (a bijection matches cards with multiplicity), so the multiset (Kelly–Ulam) version is captured, not Harary's set version. Building a literal Multiset of isomorphism classes would require transporting all cards to a common vertex type or quotienting a universe of graphs, which adds complexity without changing the mathematical content.
The minimum-order hypothesis for slot i is stated as 3 ≤ Fintype.card V only; card W = card V follows from the bijection σ inside Hypomorphic (recorded as the API lemma Hypomorphic.card_eq).
Finiteness is expressed with [Fintype V] [Fintype W]; the conjecture is false for infinite graphs (the article gives counterexamples), so restricting to finite vertex types is essential and faithful.

For slot ii, Mathlib's Digraph allows loops, so looplessness is imposed as explicit hypotheses on both digraphs (Ramachandran's digraphs are loopless with at most one arc per ordered pair; 2-cycles are allowed, and Digraph allows them). Mathlib's Digraph has at most one arc per ordered pair by construction.

Vertex-deleted subdigraphs are expressed with Mathlib's Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) (the restriction of the adjacency relation to vertices ≠ v), and digraph isomorphism is Mathlib's RelIso on adjacency relations (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj); this avoids bespoke Digraph.induce/Digraph.Iso definitions. SimpleGraph.Iso is itself a RelIso, so the two slots use the same notion of isomorphism.

Out-degree and in-degree are defined as Set.ncard of the out-/in-neighbour sets. Under the [Fintype V] hypothesis of the conjecture these are the true degrees; ncard's junk value 0 on infinite sets is never reached in the statement.

No lower bound on the number of vertices is imposed in slot ii, following Ramachandran (the degree pairs separate the two-vertex digraphs). Digraphs with 0 or 1 vertex are trivially reconstructible, so including them is harmless and faithful.

Only the two slots in the decomposition table are stated as research-open theorems; Harary's set-reconstruction and edge-reconstruction conjectures, which the list entry does not name, are deliberately not included. API/test lemmas (isomorphic ⇒ (degree-)hypomorphic, equal vertex counts, the two-vertex graphs are hypomorphic, degrees in the complete digraph) are included with full proofs to validate the bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reconstruction conjecture

The reconstruction conjecture (Kelly–Ulam) and the new digraph reconstruction conjecture
(Ramachandran) state that a finite graph, respectively a finite digraph, is determined up to
isomorphism by its vertex-deleted subgraphs.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *New digraph reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_digraph_reconstruction_conjecture)

namespace ReconstructionConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/- ## Simple graphs -/

/--
Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if they have the same *deck*, i.e. the same
multiset of isomorphism classes of vertex-deleted subgraphs. Equivalently, there is a bijection
`e` between the vertex sets such that for every vertex `v` the vertex-deleted subgraph
`G - v` (the subgraph induced on the complement of `{v}`) is isomorphic to `H - e v`.
-/
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {e v}ᶜ)

/-- Isomorphic graphs are hypomorphic. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.of_iso {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} (f : G ≃g H) :
    Hypomorphic G H :=
  ⟨f.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.subtypeEquiv f.toEquiv fun a => by simp,
    fun {a b} => f.map_adj_iff⟩⟩⟩

/-- The two graphs on two vertices are hypomorphic. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hypomorphic_bot_top_fin_two :
    Hypomorphic (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  ⟨Equiv.refl _, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.refl _, fun {a b} => by
    have ha := a.2
    have hb := b.2
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ha hb
    have : a = b := Subtype.ext (by omega)
    simp [this]⟩⟩⟩

/-- The two graphs on two vertices are not isomorphic. Together with
`hypomorphic_bot_top_fin_two`, this shows that the hypothesis of at least three vertices in
`reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i` cannot be dropped. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two :
    ¬ Nonempty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) ≃g (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2))) := by
  rintro ⟨f⟩
  have := f.map_adj_iff (v := 0) (w := 1)
  simp at this

/--
**The reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly 1957, Ulam 1960).

Any two hypomorphic finite simple graphs on at least three vertices are isomorphic. That is,
if $G$ and $H$ are finite simple graphs on at least three vertices with the same deck
(the multiset of isomorphism classes of the vertex-deleted subgraphs $G - v$), then
$G \cong H$.

The hypothesis of at least three vertices is necessary: both graphs on two vertices have the
same deck.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) (hV : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hGH : Hypomorphic G H) : Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

/- ## Digraphs

We use Mathlib's `Digraph`, which is an arbitrary relation on the vertex type: at most one arc
per ordered pair of vertices, and 2-cycles are allowed. Loops are excluded by an explicit
hypothesis. Isomorphisms of digraphs are relation isomorphisms `D.Adj ≃r E.Adj`. -/

/-- The subdigraph of the digraph `D` induced on the vertex set `s`. -/
def induceDigraph (s : Set V) (D : Digraph V) : Digraph s where
  Adj a b := D.Adj a b

/-- The out-degree of the vertex `v` in the finite digraph `D`: the number of arcs leaving `v`. -/
noncomputable def outDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard

/-- The in-degree of the vertex `v` in the finite digraph `D`: the number of arcs entering `v`. -/
noncomputable def inDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj w v}.ncard

/-- The out-degree of a vertex in a finite digraph with decidable adjacency. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_eq [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj] (v : V) :
    outDegree D v = (Finset.univ.filter fun w => D.Adj v w).card := by
  rw [outDegree, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card']
  congr 1
  ext w
  simp

/-- The in-degree of a vertex in a finite digraph with decidable adjacency. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem inDegree_eq [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj] (v : V) :
    inDegree D v = (Finset.univ.filter fun w => D.Adj w v).card := by
  rw [inDegree, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card']
  congr 1
  ext w
  simp

/--
Two digraphs `D` and `E` are **degree-hypomorphic** if they have the same
*degree-associated deck*: there is a bijection `e` between the vertex sets such that for every
vertex `v` the vertex-deleted subdigraph `D - v` is isomorphic to `E - e v`, and `v` and `e v`
have the same out-degree and the same in-degree. Equivalently, the multisets of pairs
`(D - v, (outdeg v, indeg v))`, with `D - v` taken up to isomorphism, coincide.
-/
def DegreeHypomorphic (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : V ≃ W, ∀ v,
    Nonempty ((induceDigraph {v}ᶜ D).Adj ≃r (induceDigraph {e v}ᶜ E).Adj) ∧
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (e v) ∧ inDegree D v = inDegree E (e v)

/-- Isomorphic digraphs are degree-hypomorphic. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem DegreeHypomorphic.of_iso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (f : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) :
    DegreeHypomorphic D E := by
  refine ⟨f.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨⟨Equiv.subtypeEquiv f.toEquiv fun a => by simp,
    fun {a b} => f.map_rel_iff⟩⟩, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [outDegree, outDegree,
      ← Set.ncard_image_of_injective {w | D.Adj v w} f.injective]
    congr 1
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
      exact f.map_rel_iff.mpr hu
    · intro h
      exact ⟨f.symm w, by rw [← f.map_rel_iff, f.apply_symm_apply]; exact h,
        f.apply_symm_apply w⟩
  · rw [inDegree, inDegree,
      ← Set.ncard_image_of_injective {w | D.Adj w v} f.injective]
    congr 1
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
      exact f.map_rel_iff.mpr hu

# Reconstruction conjecture

The *deck* of a finite graph $G$ is the multiset of isomorphism classes of its vertex-deleted
subgraphs $G - v$ (one *card* for each vertex $v$). Two graphs with the same deck are
*hypomorphic*. The **reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly, Ulam) says that any two hypomorphic
graphs on at least three vertices are isomorphic.

The analogous statement for digraphs is false (Stockmeyer). The **new digraph reconstruction
conjecture** (Ramachandran, 1981) is the weaker statement in which each card $D - v$ is
labelled with the degree pair $(\operatorname{od}(v), \operatorname{id}(v))$ of the deleted
vertex: any two digraphs with the same degree-associated deck are isomorphic.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Reconstruction conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, New digraph reconstruction conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_digraph_reconstruction_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* Kelly, P. J. (1957), "A congruence theorem for trees", *Pacific J. Math.* 7, 961–968.
* Ramachandran, S. (1981), "On a new digraph reconstruction conjecture",
  *J. Combin. Theory Ser. B* 31, 143–149.
* [McKay, B. D. (2022), "Reconstruction of small graphs and digraphs",

-/

variable {V W : Type*}

/-
## Simple graphs

The vertex-deleted subgraph $G - v$ is the induced subgraph `G.induce {v}ᶜ`. Since the cards of
$G$ are indexed by the vertices of $G$, two graphs have the same deck (as a *multiset* of
isomorphism classes) exactly when there is a bijection $\sigma$ between their vertex sets with
$G - v \cong H - \sigma(v)$ for every vertex $v$. This is the usual definition of a
hypomorphism.
-/

/-- Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if they have the same deck, i.e. there is a
bijection `σ` between their vertex sets such that `G - v` is isomorphic to `H - σ v` for every
vertex `v` of `G`. -/
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ)

/-- The two graphs on two vertices are hypomorphic (but not isomorphic), so the hypothesis
"at least three vertices" in the reconstruction conjecture cannot be dropped. -/

  refine ⟨Equiv.refl _, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.refl _, fun {a b} => ?_⟩⟩⟩
  have hab : a = b := by
    ext
    have ha := a.2
    have hb := b.2
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ha hb
    omega
  subst hab
  simp

finite simple graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of
isomorphism classes of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. -/

## Digraphs

A digraph is loopless and has at most one arc for each ordered pair of vertices; both arcs
`u → v` and `v → u` may be present. We model these as `Digraph V` (Mathlib's `Digraph` allows

relation isomorphism `D.Adj ≃r E.Adj`.

/-- The vertex-deleted subdigraph `D - v`: the subdigraph of `D` induced on the vertices other
than `v`. -/
def deleteVertex (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : Digraph {w // w ≠ v} where
  Adj a b := D.Adj a b

/-- The **out-degree** of a vertex `v` of the digraph `D`: the number of arcs leaving `v`. -/
noncomputable def outDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard

/-- The **in-degree** of a vertex `v` of the digraph `D`: the number of arcs entering `v`. -/
noncomputable def inDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj w v}.ncard

  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty ((deleteVertex D v).Adj ≃r (deleteVertex E (σ v)).Adj) ∧

  Adj i j := i = 0 ∧ j = 1

Two finite simple graphs have the same deck if their vertex-deleted induced subgraphs can be
matched, with multiplicity, so that matched subgraphs are isomorphic.
-/
def SameDeck {V W : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : V ≃ W, ∀ v : V,
    Nonempty (G.induce {w | w ≠ v} ≃g H.induce {w | w ≠ e v})

/--
The Kelly--Ulam reconstruction conjecture: any two finite simple graphs on at least three
vertices whose multisets of isomorphism classes of single-vertex-deleted induced subgraphs are
equal are isomorphic. The lower bound of three is essential.
-/

theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i :
    ∀ {V W : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype W] (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W),
      3 ≤ Fintype.card V → SameDeck G H → Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

/-- The induced digraph on a set of vertices. -/
def induceDigraph {V : Type*} (G : Digraph V) (s : Set V) : Digraph s where
  Adj v w := G.Adj v w

/-- The number of arcs directed out of a vertex of a finite digraph. -/
noncomputable def outDegree {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | G.Adj v w}.ncard

/-- The number of arcs directed into a vertex of a finite digraph. -/
noncomputable def inDegree {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=

/-- Two digraphs are isomorphic when an equivalence of vertices preserves and reflects arcs. -/
def DigraphIsomorphic {V W : Type*} (G : Digraph V) (H : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (RelIso G.Adj H.Adj)

vertices have the same ordered pair (outdegree, indegree). This matching retains multiplicity.

**The reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly–Ulam).

the cards $G - v$ over all vertices $v$ of $G$. Two graphs with the same deck are *hypomorphic*.

if there is a bijection `φ : V ≃ W` between their vertex sets such that `G - v ≅ H - φ v` for
every vertex `v`. The hypothesis is stated in this form. Requiring only the same *set* of cards
would give Harary's stronger set reconstruction conjecture, which is not stated here.

The hypothesis $|V(G)| \ge 3$ is necessary: the two graphs on two vertices have the same deck but
are not isomorphic (see `two_vertex_graphs_hypomorphic_not_iso`).

    Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

vertices, so $2$-cycles (arcs in both directions between two vertices) are allowed. For a vertex
$v$ of a digraph $D$, the *degree-associated card* of $v$ is the pair

vertex-deleted subdigraph $D - v$ together with the out-degree and the in-degree of $v$ in $D$.

vertices $v$ of $D$.

through a bijection `φ : V ≃ W` such that, for every vertex `v`, the subdigraphs `D - v` and

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reconstruction conjectures

The graph reconstruction conjecture concerns the multiset of induced subgraphs obtained by deleting
one vertex. The new digraph reconstruction conjecture instead uses the degree-associated deck.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Reconstruction conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
-/

namespace ReconstructionConjecture

/--
**Kelly–Ulam reconstruction conjecture.** Any two finite simple graphs, each on at least three
vertices, are isomorphic if their decks are equal. Here deck equality means that there is a
bijection between the vertex-deleted induced subgraphs, counted with multiplicity, which pairs
isomorphic cards.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i :
    ∀ {V W : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype W] (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W),
      3 ≤ Fintype.card V →
      3 ≤ Fintype.card W →
      (∃ e : V ≃ W, ∀ v : V,
        Nonempty (G.induce ({v}ᶜ : Set V) ≃g H.induce ({e v}ᶜ : Set W))) →
      Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

/--
**New digraph reconstruction conjecture (Ramachandran, 1981).** Every finite loopless digraph is
determined up to isomorphism by its degree-associated deck: the multiset of pairs consisting of
the vertex-deleted induced digraph and the deleted vertex's ordered pair (out-degree, in-degree).
There is no minimum number of vertices. Digraphs have at most one arc for each ordered pair and may
contain directed $2$-cycles.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.ii :
    ∀ {V W : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype W] (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W),
      Irreflexive D.Adj →
      Irreflexive E.Adj →
      (∃ e : V ≃ W, ∀ v : V,
        Nonempty
          ((fun x y : {w : V // w ≠ v} => D.Adj x.1 y.1) ≃r
            (fun x y : {w : W // w ≠ e v} => E.Adj x.1 y.1)) ∧
        (Set.ncard {w : V | D.Adj v w}, Set.ncard {w : V | D.Adj w v}) =
          (Set.ncard {w : W | E.Adj (e v) w}, Set.ncard {w : W | E.Adj w (e v)})) →
      Nonempty (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) := by
  sorry

end ReconstructionConjecture
modeling_decisions: For the Kelly–Ulam conjecture, equality of multiset decks is encoded by an equivalence between the two vertex types together with an isomorphism between the corresponding single-vertex-deleted induced cards. The equivalence matches card occurrences, so repeated isomorphism classes retain their multiplicity.
Simple graphs are represented by Mathlib's `SimpleGraph`; both finite vertex types are explicitly required to have cardinality at least three.

For the new digraph reconstruction conjecture, a digraph is Mathlib's relation-valued `Digraph`. `Irreflexive D.Adj` imposes looplessness; relation-valued adjacency already has at most one arc per ordered pair, and no asymmetry condition is imposed, so directed 2-cycles are allowed.
A vertex-deleted digraph is represented by restricting adjacency to the subtype of vertices unequal to the deleted vertex. Directed graph isomorphism is represented by `RelIso`.

Equality of degree-associated multiset decks is encoded by a bijection of card occurrences matching both the deleted digraph up to isomorphism and the ordered pair (out-degree, in-degree). Degrees are the `Set.ncard` of the corresponding outgoing and incoming neighbor sets in the original digraph.
No minimum-order hypothesis is imposed on the digraph conjecture, including for empty, one-vertex, and two-vertex finite digraphs.
